data.headline: DVM, MBA, DACVP | pursuing PhD in Bioinformatics | Preclinical Pathologist | Digital & AI Strategy in Pathology | Matrixed Team Leader
data.about: Board certified veterinary pathologist applying digital pathology and computational methods to discovery and safety assessment across diagnostics, large biopharma, and contract research settings. My background includes leadership roles across the industry, with a focus on integrating computational tools into preclinical and translational pathology workflows.Currently pursuing a PhD in bioinformatics and computational biology to strengthen the connection between morphological findings and molecular data, supporting more precise and therapeutically relevant outcomes.

description.text: As Director of Discovery and Digital Pathology, I lead the integration of advanced imaging and quantitative tissue analytics into nonclinical discovery and efficacy. My focus is on deploying digital pathology and spatial biology platforms to extract objective endpoints from complex tissue sections. I manage a cross-functional team of pathologists and imaging scientists, and collaborate with data science units to combine morphological data with molecular datasets, aligning across the discovery portfolio.

subComponents.title: Sr. Manager, Global PRL Pathology Services
subComponents.caption: Jul 2024 - Sep 2025 · 1 yr 2 mos

description.text:
• Lead and manage a team of 13 pathology and clinical professionals, overseeing operations and serving as the primary veterinary pathologist on preclinical and medical device studies.

• Drive financial optimization and calculated risk strategies to develop new revenue streams for the pathology group, ensuring sustainable growth.

• Initiate the development of a digital and computational pathology database, laying the foundation for AI/ML model integration in medical device pathology.

• Generate Annual Operating Plans (AOPs) and optimize expenses, balancing cost efficiency with high-quality pathology services to enhance operational effectiveness.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with business leaders to identify and bring new lines of business in-house, expanding pathology service capabilities and market reach.

• Redesign internal workflows and team structures to streamline pathology operations, improving turnaround time and resource utilization.

• Implement data-driven process improvements that increase operational efficiency, reduce redundancies, and align the pathology team with broader organizational goals.

• Serve as the primary veterinary pathologist for GLP and non-GLP studies, focusing on cardiac pathology across various large animal models, including rabbits, dogs, sheep, and pigs.

• Collaborate with study directors and scientists to design and refine protocols, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and study objectives.

 • Lead the development of a telepathology system to support remote pathologists, enhancing accessibility and efficiency in necropsy and histopathologic evaluations.

 • Utilize digital pathology software to generate precise histomorphometric data, providing sponsors with accurate, quantitative pathology insights.

 • Apply expertise in ISO 10993 and work with the FDA to guide the development of digital pathology regulations, ensuring compliance and innovation in medical device pathology.

• Led and managed a team of 16 veterinary pathologists, providing mentorship, performance oversight, and professional development opportunities to enhance team effectiveness.

• Identified and elevated a team member into a leadership position, fostering growth and strengthening leadership within the pathology department.

• Spearheaded digital and computational pathology advancements, collaborating with cross-functional teams to drive innovation and improve diagnostic efficiency.

• Developed a strategic business plan for a new pathology role, aimed at reducing subject matter expert (SME) burden and optimizing workflow efficiency.

• It Partnered with key stakeholders to align pathology operations with business objectives, ensuring high-quality diagnostic services and sustainable growth with financial optimization.

• Performed microscopic and gross pathology evaluations on surgical biopsy and necropsy specimens, with a focus on hepatic and neoplastic pathology, to provide accurate diagnoses.

• Interpreted and reported pathology findings for clinical and research purposes, ensuring high diagnostic accuracy and clear communication with veterinarians and specialists.

• Collaborated with clinicians and researchers to support case management, treatment decisions, and advancements in veterinary surgical pathology.

• Provided expert consultation on histopathologic interpretation of hepatic and respiratory diseases, aiding in the diagnosis and prognosis of complex cases.

experiences.caption: Jul 2018 - Jan 2020 · 1 yr 6 mos

description.text: Collections-based, digital pathology and image analysis focused, histopathologic characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infected Common marmosets, rabbits, and rodents utilizing image analysis software to generate quantitative data that can be correlated to the radiologic signature - in an effort to create the ‘virtual biopsy’ for pulmonary tuberculosis. The regular review, interoperation, and drafting reports concerning the toxicopathologic effects of anti-tuberculosis compounds on various animals, composing technical summaries of my findings. Major accomplishments include the development of a novel in-situ hybridization probe for the marmoset, and development of an image analysis algorithm to detect spatiality of the probe in tissue.

experiences.title: Veterinary anatomic pathology resident
experiences.subtitle: Michigan State University College of Veterinary Medicine . undefined
experiences.caption: Jul 2016 - Jun 2019 · 2 yrs 11 mos

description.text: Engaged in a leadership role through the regular review, interpretation, and analysis of over 2000 surgical biopsy cases and 1000 gross necropsy cases, and guided teams of veterinary students through initial gross necropsy findings, histologic interpretation, and pathogenesis of disease. Regularly communicated pathologic findings to referring clinicians, private clients, and stakeholders in the agriculture and food sectors. Regularly participated in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) surveillance with epidemiologists and the local Department of Natural Resources, and routinely interpreted and reported pathology data as it related to human exposure, food safety, and veterinary defense. Researched and published the immunohistochemical characteristics of extranodal follicular lymphoma in the dog.

Created a novel diabetic guinea pig model utilizing streptozotocin and developed a clinical monitoring program for long-term maintenance of the model. Characterized the in-vitro effect of advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) on Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) through the use of Mtb cell culture, mass spectrometry, and flow cytometry. Regularly engaged in outreach activities through student mentorship, public health outreach within the local community, and writing technical data in an easy to read essay format for community education.

description.text: Created a novel diabetic rabbit model utilizing alloxan and developed a clinical monitoring program for long-term maintenance of the model. Reviewed, interpreted, and reported histopathologic findings in diabetic rabbits infected with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). Coordinated activities with the animal care team, and assisted in the creation of new protocols and procedures regarding the risks of human exposure to contagious and infectious diseases. Routinely reviewed, assessed, and interpreted complex and sensitive scientific data as it related to treatment of Mtb, and developed a communication strategy to coordinate with relevant stakeholders.

Assisted in the development of written protocols and policies regarding surgical procedures in immune-compromised animals, and performed xenograft implantation in a sterile environment for such animals. Performed gross necropsies on cohorts of on-study animals and assisted in the histopathologic evaluation. Routinely performed rtPCR, ELISA, and gel electrophoresis, and collated such data into easy-to-read tables and figures. Routinely coordinated activities between intra- and extramural stakeholders to ensure effective communication of relevant results as it related to the scientific study and pathology data.

•	Novel compound administration and blood draws via the Culex automated sampling machine
•	Designed an in-situ liver perfusion technique in the rat animal model

•	Phenotyping transgenic animals of interest for continued metabolic study via GTT, OGTT, ITT, and AIS 
•	Necropsy and sample collection used for genotyping and histology
